Stephanie / Alicia — looping in legal-context comments from our side. Below are suggested, concise edits we typically use to balance customer assurance and operational constraints.

Suggested exhibit language (high level):
"Redwood will maintain SOC 2 Type II attestation for the Security Trust Services Criteria and shall provide Customer with a redacted copy of the report upon execution of a mutual NDA. For clarifications, Redwood will provide a one-page SOC 2 summary and a SOC 2 cover page within five (5) business days of request."

Audit/pen test clause (suggestion):
"Customer may, no more than once per 12 months, engage a mutually agreeable third-party auditor to perform a remote security assessment of Redwood's production environment subject to the parties agreeing in writing to a scope and schedule at least thirty (30) days prior to the assessment. Remote assessments shall be limited to non-intrusive testing. For on-site audits, the parties shall negotiate scope, timing and costs in good faith."

Evidence cadence (operational proposal):
- Quarterly bundle (standard): redacted SOC 2 summary, change-log for infra/system updates, dashboard screenshots of key controls, redacted token-level usage logs for sampled windows.
- Incident bundle (trigger-based): within 14 business days provide incident report, affected control evidence, and mitigation steps.

Notes: we shy away from unconstrained "audit rights" language (e.g., unlimited access or unfettered on-site inspections). Thirty (30) days' notice gives us time to coordinate tooling access + legal approvals. We can accept a shorter notice for remote evidence requests (10 business days) if Helix agrees to keep requests scoped.

I'll bring a tracked-change draft to the call.

-Karthik

1) Remote authenticated testing: Redwood will agree to mutually scoped authenticated remote testing limited to a pre-agreed test plan and performed by a mutually acceptable vendor or resource. We will not accept intrusive, destructive tests that could risk multi-tenant stability.
